name: ASML’s 0.55 NA EXE EUV platform
description: ASML’s 0.55 NA scanner family extended 13.5 nm EUV patterning to finer features, with experimental patterning at imec and subsequent production qualification on selected Intel 18A layers.

date.basis: Date or date granularity stated in the cited source.

events.statement: ASML delivered its first High-NA EUV lithography system.
events.caveats: A delivery is not itself completed installation or process qualification.

evidence.locator: Mass producing leading-edge microchips and Developing EUV lithography
evidence.supports: ASML identifies the first High-NA delivery date.
The supplier distinguishes the subsequent Intel integration in 2024 from later production qualification.

date.label: by 7 August 2024
date.basis: The 7 August release presents test patterns printed before publication.

events.statement: Imec published single-exposure logic and DRAM test structures patterned on the EXE:5000 at the joint imec–ASML development lab.
events.place_note: The exposure site was Veldhoven, even though the release has a Leuven dateline.
events.caveats: This is a patterning demonstration on test structures.

evidence.locator: Opening description and Steven Scheer statement
evidence.supports: Identifies 0.55 NA test structures, fine logic patterns, and the Veldhoven exposure site.

evidence.locator: Main paragraph 1, lab opening and prototype
evidence.supports: Identifies the working development site and its EXE:5000 prototype.

date.label: by 24 February 2025
date.basis: Release date bounds the electrical test results presented by imec.

events.statement: Imec obtained electrical results from 20 nm pitch metal-line test structures printed using single-exposure High-NA EUV.
events.caveats: Test-structure electrical yield is a different milestone from yield on volume customer products.

evidence.supports: Reports the test vehicle and electrical-yield evidence.

date.label: by 18 March 2026
date.basis: The public announcement confirms arrival at the development facility by this date.

events.statement: Imec received an EXE:5200 scanner at its Leuven pilot facility.
events.caveats: Full tool qualification was expected by Q4 2026. The delivery announcement does not establish its completion.

evidence.supports: Imec reports tool arrival and gives a prospective qualification target.

date.label: by 15 July 2026
date.basis: The 15 July announcement reports wafer processing and customer shipments already underway.

events.statement: Intel qualified High-NA alongside the NXE platform on selected layers of a subset of Panther Lake processors made on Intel 18A and shipped products to customers.
events.place_note: Oregon, United States. The source does not name a production room.
events.caveats: The sources do not give the fraction of processors or the number of production wafers. September’s cumulative count also covers research and certification.

evidence.locator: Summary bullets, Intel statement and tool history
evidence.supports: ASML names the dual-qualified layers, customer shipments and Oregon.

evidence.locator: Exhibit 99.1, Business Highlights, Intel Foundry bullet
evidence.supports: Intel’s results filing corroborates the EXE high-volume adoption and product subset.
The September update corroborates that select-layer commercial production continued at that date.

earliest_record.rationale: The first equipment delivery is the earliest dated entry for the EXE platform in the retained sources. Later events capture test, delivery and production separately.

research.note: The grain is the EXE platform, with recipient and production-use events, rather than a separate node for each delivery or adopting fab.

links.statement: EXE retains the 13.5 nm wavelength of the 0.33 NA NXE generation and raises numerical aperture to 0.55 with new optics and related patterning changes.
links.scope: Optical and process evolution within ASML’s EUV platform family.

evidence.locator: Mass producing leading-edge microchips and Developing EUV lithography
evidence.supports: ASML compares the two platforms’ common EUV wavelength and different numerical apertures.

evidence.locator: The start of the EUV era and The next big thing: High NA EUV
evidence.supports: The development user describes new optics and changes to materials and processing needed to move beyond 0.33 NA.

links.caveats: Different apertures are complementary for selected layers. Intel’s dual qualification confirms one concrete example of overlap.
